attributes.residual: THE FR UNPARK CONDITION IS REFUTED, AND THE THREE PAD FAILURES ARE NOW EXPLAINED. (1) REFUTATION: FR recommended 'eliminate the six memory temporaries entirely by respelling the six FloatBits and-mask operations so their results stay in registers' as the genuinely untried axis. The TARGET EMITS THE SAME SIX MEMORY TEMPORARIES. Read straight off `fnasm.py game/game/combat.c someone_will_be_off_screen`: the target stores/reloads its union round-trips at 56/60/64/68/72/76(r1) with exactly our stfs -> lwz -> (and) -> stw -> lfs shape at 16/20/24/28/36/40(r1), and every one of those words sits in an EQUAL run of the matcher (they appear as IMMEDIATE rows, opcode agreeing, only the r1 displacement differing). Eliminating them would delete roughly 24 instructions the target HAS and break the held T199/O199 parity. The axis is not merely untried, it is WRONG-DIRECTIONED; do not execute it. (2) FULLER FRAME MAP, both sides, read from the epilogue `addi r1,r1,232`, `stmw r22,128(r1)` and the `_savefpr_24` idiom: frame 232 on both sides, saved GPRs r22-r31 at 128..167, saved FPRs at 168..231, so the LOCAL AREA IS 8..127 on both sides (FR's map stopped at 103 and therefore mis-split the dead bytes). TARGET: 48 bytes never referenced at 8..55; the temp pool (six 4-use f32 slots plus TWO s16[2] buffers) at 56..87; 16 bytes of declared local at 88..103; three f64 int-to-float magic-constant temporaries at 104/112/120. OURS: 8 bytes never referenced at 8..15; the pool (six f32 slots plus ONE s16[2]) at 16..43; stackLayout[56] at 48..103; the SAME three f64 temporaries at 104/112/120. The f64 temps and the saved-register areas already agree exactly. (3) WHY THE PAD PROBES COULD NEVER WORK, measured independently here: probe B added ONE scalar pointer local and the frame grew 232 -> 240 with the f64 temps pushed up 8 bytes while THE POOL BASE STAYED AT 16. Declared locals are allocated ABOVE the pool and never below it, so no declaration order, count or size of declared pads can put 40 dead bytes beneath the pool. That is a fourth independent confirmation of FR's negative result and, unlike FR's, it names the mechanism. (4) THE TRUE UNPARK CONDITION, correctly scoped at last: the only frame region below the temp pool is the outgoing parameter area, so the target's pool base of 56 requires a 48-byte outgoing parameter area against our 8. Both streams call MBWindowProject with exactly four register arguments (r3/r4/r5/r6 at target 0xa0-0xb4) and no stack arguments, and both call MBScreenHeight/MBScreenWidth with none, so no call in either stream explains 40 bytes of argument space. Finding what sizes that area at 48 bytes IS the whole remaining residual for this function.

hypothesis.statement: The entire remaining residual reduces to one question: what makes MWCC size this function's outgoing parameter area at 48 bytes instead of 8? Candidates, in cost order: (a) a callee prototype that passes an aggregate BY VALUE, which would reserve argument space without changing the four-register call sequence; (b) an inlined callee whose own outgoing parameter area merges into this frame; (c) an unprototyped/varargs declaration form for MBWindowProject that makes MWCC reserve home space for its arguments. Establish the parameter-area size first, and the pool base, the two s16[2] buffers and all 34 displacement rows follow by construction.
